_format: Every visible string on the site. Sections: 'shell' (every page), 'components' (component display names), and one section per page id under 'pages'.
Inside a section, keys are flat names; a dot is part of the name, not nesting (the spec has both 'tile.headcount' and 'tile.headcount.asof').
Each section has a sibling '_status' map giving every key in that section a status: 'signed' or 'unsigned'. Only signed strings may ship.

Signed: see each section's _status. Sources: Workforce size spec section 4 (D-030), Hiring and departures spec section 4 (D-040, including the shell rate keys ctl.rate*, ctl.rate.help.* and chart.noRateAtGrain), Who is leaving spec section 5 (D-044), Components compared spec section 5 (D-047), Workforce Look-Up spec section 4 (D-056), Reading the data spec section 2 (D-050; its rates.reasons table row is split into the series labels plus per-reason keys rates.reasons.<column>, text as written), component display names (D-016), series labels (D-015, D-020; docs/metric-spec.md section 4), grain control (D-033), job series filter keys and series names (D-063; 'series_names' holds the 15 names by code, shown as 'Name (code)'), shell copy (D-034, D-035).

Shared keys live in 'shell': flag.provisional, ctl.component and ctl.component.all (signed with the Workforce size spec, D-030) and flag.smallBase and flag.ytd (signed with the Hiring and departures spec, D-040) are used by every data page. The 'series' section holds the signed category and hire-type labels, keyed by cube column.
The draft badge shows on a page while any key that page uses is unsigned.

Administrations addendum (docs/pages/administrations.md section 4, D-068): its keys live in 'shell' (the presets, period labels, rate note and Compare administrations panel appear on several pages), except ctl.view.admin, which is on the Who is leaving page beside ctl.view.t12. The date-range presets are built in code from the D-065 windows (assets/js/admin.js) with the admin.* labels under ctl.presets.label; the old unsigned hook keys ctl.range.presets and ctl.range.presetsLabel are removed.

The Compare administrations panel also shows signed strings of the Components compared page by reference (components-compared:col.hires, col.departures, col.rate, col.quit, col.retirement) for its series names and table columns, rather than duplicating them.

Redesign (docs/pages/redesign.md section 7, D-072): its keys live in 'shell', since the three main pages (Overview, Departures, Components; page ids overview, departures, components-view) share the control bar, tiles and navigation. Those pages have no page section of their own: their h1 is shell:nav.* and the document title is taken from the h1. The old pages live on unchanged as history-*.html (their page sections unchanged), shown inside 'Explore full history'. The new pages also show signed strings of the old pages by reference where the spec reuses them (group labels, panel titles, the unknown and not-applicable lines, coverage, series names of hires and departures).

D-074 adds shell dep.who.unknownAdmin and dep.who.coverageAdmin (Departures Chart C notes, one per administration shown); D-075 adds shell comp.minis.title and comp.minis.note (the Components mini charts; also in docs/pages/redesign.md section 7).
D-076 adds shell comp.minis.crsNote (Community Relations Service's mini chart on its own scale) and dep.who.unknownAdmin1 (the singular Unknown line).
D-077: shell tile.rateSince and tile.drpSince shortened; adds comp.chart.crsNote, comp.minis.value, adm.ruleN (the month-N rule's label) and adm.tipMonth (the months-in-office tooltip title).
D-078 adds shell ctl.components.n, ctl.components.header, ctl.components.all and sel.components (the component multi-select on the main pages).

D-081 adds shell comp.minis.expand, comp.minis.close, comp.minis.year and comp.minis.xTitle (the Components mini charts' Expand button and dialog, the small charts' year ticks and the expanded chart's x-axis title).

D-080 adds shell reasons.drpNote (the note under every "Why people left" chart: Departures, the Compare administrations panel, and the Hiring and departures and Components compared pages under Explore full history), replacing hiring-and-departures chart.reasons.drpNote there; DRP is the seventh reason, labeled with the signed series:sep_drp.

D-083 replaces reading-the-data rates.p5 with Cary's signed wording (DRP as its own reason in the reasons charts) and removes hiring-and-departures chart.reasons.drp and chart.reasons.drpNote, unused since D-080; the spec tables in docs/pages/reading-the-data.md and hiring-and-departures.md match.

Appointments (docs/pages/appointments.md section 7, D-086 as amended by D-085): its 25 keys live in 'shell' (nav.appointments is in the navigation on every page; the page, id appointments, has no page section of its own, like the other main pages). The page also reuses signed strings by reference: shell:tile.employees and shell:compare.change.pct label the Count and Share choice of the workforce-mix chart, and hiring-and-departures:chart.flows.series.hires and .departures name the bars.

reading-the-data.page.title: Reading the data
reading-the-data.page.intro: Breaking down data sourcing, caveats and best tips in analysis. Figures on this page are as of the July 2026 data.
reading-the-data.toc.label: On this page
reading-the-data.source.title: Source and coverage
reading-the-data.source.p1: All figures come from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's Federal Workforce Data. OPM publishes two types of monthly files: a snapshot of total payroll at the end of each month, and a record of personnel actions, including hires and departures.
reading-the-data.source.p2: Dashboard data begins in October 2011 and goes through the latest month OPM has published. Justice Connection updates the dashboard when OPM releases new data, which lags by about a month.
reading-the-data.source.p3: "Justice Department" means every component of the Department. Files before January 2015 identify the Department differently; we use the matching code, and the employee count is continuous across the change (114,656 in December 2014, 114,163 in January 2015).
reading-the-data.source.p4: The Department's components are shown as OPM reports them. The Community Relations Service was eliminated in April 2026; OPM's files show no CRS employees after that month, so it is shown with 0 employees, hires and departures from May 2026. It is also missing from OPM's January 2026 file, so that month shows 0 employees.
reading-the-data.source.p5: Each record is one person, but OPM's files have no personal identifier, so the dashboard cannot follow an individual from month to month.
reading-the-data.counting.title: Data breakdown
reading-the-data.counting.p1: Employees: the number of people in the month-end snapshot. For a quarter or a year, we show the count at the end of its last month, never an average or a sum.
reading-the-data.counting.p2: Hires and departures: counted in the month the action took effect, not the month OPM processed it. Most actions appear in the file for the month they took effect; since 2020, 98.7% appear within one month.
reading-the-data.counting.p3: Provisional: because some actions arrive late, the newest three months can still change and are marked as provisional.
reading-the-data.counting.p4: Years are organized from October to September following the federal fiscal year. A year or quarter that is still in progress is marked partial and covers only the months published so far.
reading-the-data.counting.p5: Change in employees and hires minus departures are counted from different files, so they do not always match. We show both and do not adjust one to fit the other. In most years they differ by less than 500.
reading-the-data.rates.title: Rates and categories
reading-the-data.rates.p1: A departure rate is the number of people who left, divided by the average number of employees over the same months. The average is taken over month-end counts. Quit and retirement rates work the same way, counting only those reasons.
reading-the-data.rates.p2: You can choose how the rate is measured:
reading-the-data.rates.list.a: Last 12 months: departures in the 12 months up to each point, over the average employee count in those months.
reading-the-data.rates.list.b: Fiscal year: departures in each fiscal year, over its average employee count. A year still in progress shows the year so far.
reading-the-data.rates.list.c: Annual pace: departures in each period, scaled up to a full year, over the period's average employee count.
reading-the-data.rates.p3: Small groups: when a rate is based on fewer than 30 employees on average, it is shown with a flag. Such rates can swing widely from one period to the next; they are shown, not hidden.
reading-the-data.rates.p4: Every departure falls into exactly one reason, based on OPM's separation codes:
reading-the-data.rates.p5: Deferred Resignation Program (DRP): OPM flags departures under the program from March 2025. In the reasons charts they are shown as their own reason and are not counted again under Quit, Retirement or the other reasons; the tiles and rate lines still count them under their original reason.
reading-the-data.rates.p6: Hires are either new hires (competitive, excepted or Senior Executive Service appointments) or transfers in from another agency.
reading-the-data.rates.p7: Who is leaving groups people by years of service, age (OPM's brackets), supervisory role and occupation. Groups are shown only by fiscal year or for 12-month periods, never month by month, so that small groups do not point to individuals. People whose group is unknown are counted in totals but not shown as a group.
reading-the-data.gaps.title: Known gaps and data issues
reading-the-data.gaps.drp.title: The Deferred Resignation Program gap (fiscal years 2025 and 2026)
reading-the-data.gaps.drp.p1: About 4,800 departures took effect in September 2025, most of them under the Deferred Resignation Program, but the employee count fell mostly in October 2025 (by 3,860). As a result, change in employees and hires minus departures differ by about 4,000 in each of fiscal years 2025 and 2026, in opposite directions. Across the two years the difference largely cancels out.
reading-the-data.gaps.los.title: Length of service recorded from 1900
reading-the-data.gaps.los.p1: In OPM's departure files for June 2024 through July 2025, some records show about 125 years of service: the time since 1 January 1900 rather than since the person's start date. This affects 39 Justice Department departures between October 2024 and March 2025. We treat those values as unknown: they are left out of years of experience lost, and the coverage shown next to that figure reflects it. The Look-Up shows OPM's values as published.
reading-the-data.gaps.occ.title: Occupational category missing
reading-the-data.gaps.occ.p1: From June 2024, OPM's departure files no longer fill in the broad occupational category. We group occupations by OPM's job series instead (attorneys 0905, criminal investigators 1811, correctional officers 0007).
reading-the-data.gaps.redact.title: Pay and location withheld
reading-the-data.gaps.redact.p1: OPM withholds pay and duty location for many employees: about two thirds of Justice Department records, and 79% to 90% at the FBI, DEA, U.S. Marshals Service, ATF and the U.S. Attorneys' offices. The dashboard therefore does not show pay or location breakdowns.
reading-the-data.gaps.revisions.title: Revised files
reading-the-data.gaps.revisions.p1: OPM sometimes reissues a month's files. When that happens we reload them, and months whose files changed are flagged. Figures on the dashboard can change as a result.
